about.title: Home
about.subtitle: BI, Fabric & Power Platform developer and consultant with 4 years of experience in data
about.greeting: Hi, I’m Michał — I turn data into decisions.
about.p1: I design and deliver data solutions across the Microsoft stack: from architecture in Microsoft Fabric, through semantic models and Power BI reports, to Power Apps with Power Automate. I work with B2B clients — from large corporations to small companies — and own the whole project cycle: business workshops, delivery and handover to the client's team. I lead a small implementation team: I plan the work, split the tasks and keep the quality high. Before that I was a data analyst in an international team at Novartis. After hours I mentor 1:1 in Power BI, SQL and data modeling.

me.title: About me
me.subtitle: Outside of work — the things that fold me into shape

intro.p1: I have always been pulled in two directions: towards science subjects and towards creating things. For a long time they seemed like separate worlds — until I found Business Intelligence, where one doesn't work without the other. That's how working with data became not just my job, but a passion.
intro.p2: Outside of work, too, I enjoy most what mixes curiosity with imagination. Here are the three things that take up most of my free time.

space.title: Science & space
space.p1: Space has fascinated me for as long as I can remember. The spark was Stephen Hawking’s “A Brief History of Time” — black holes, the beginning of the Universe, the nature of time. But it was Richard Feynman who showed me that even the greatest theories can be boiled down to simple associations, and that you can build real intuition on them — no PhD in physics required.
space.p2: Then came “Interstellar” and Kip Thorne’s “The Science of Interstellar” — the physicist who didn't just advise on the film, but actually computed what Gargantua would look like. To this day my favourite moment is when a complicated equation turns into a picture you can stand in awe of. I remember Gargantua filling me with wonder and dread at once — at how beautiful and how merciless it was.
space.hint: Move the cursor — this is how a black hole bends starlight

stories.title: Books & games
stories.p1: Books and games are first of all entertainment for me — fantasy, a good plot, worlds you want to come back to. I like the ones that bring a bit of philosophy along with the adventure and leave you wondering what being human actually means.

gravel.title: Gravel
gravel.p1: For me, sport is above all a way to switch off. After a day full of meetings, models and measures I get on the gravel bike and just ride — dirt roads, forest tracks, back lanes. An hour or two later my head is clear and the energy is back.
gravel.p2: Sometimes the laptop comes along too. Clients like hearing their project is out of the woods — they don't need to know the email was sent from the middle of them.
gravel.alt: A gravel bike leaning on a bench in a forest shelter, with a laptop and a backpack on the table

story.title: The Beginning
story.description: Every journey starts with curiosity. Mine began with late nights, endless questions, and the relentless pursuit of turning ideas into reality. This is where passion meets purpose.

stories.title: Curiosity & Passion
stories.description: Every project starts with curiosity — questions that won’t let go and ideas that demand to be built. It’s what drives me to experiment and look for new ways forward.

stories.title: Creating & Growing
stories.description: Countless hours spent coding, exploring data, and solving problems taught me that challenges are opportunities to learn. Each project has sharpened my skills and deepened my understanding of the analytical process.

stories.title: Insight & Impact
stories.description: Data isn’t just numbers — it’s stories waiting to be uncovered. Over time I’ve learned how to turn complex information into clear insights that shape better decisions.

stories.title: Ready for Challenges
stories.description: I adapt quickly to new situations and thrive under pressure. I see challenges as a chance to push past limits and keep questioning the status quo.

journey.title: Journey
journey.subtitle: Professional and educational path I have taken

timelineData.title: Developer & Consultant: BI, Fabric, Power Platform — Clickless / Odczaruj Power BI
timelineData.description: I lead end-to-end BI projects for B2B clients — from the largest corporations to small businesses — working with Paweł Czapiewski at Odczaruj Power BI and Clickless. I own the whole cycle: requirements workshops, data architecture in Microsoft Fabric, semantic models and Power BI reports, and Power Apps (canvas and model-driven) on Dataverse with Power Automate. I also run 1:1 mentoring and support courses, helping analysts master Power BI, SQL and data modeling. I also lead a small implementation team: I plan the work, distribute tasks and own the quality of the delivered solutions.
timelineData.label: Clickless / Odczaruj Power BI

timelineData.title: Freelance BI & Microsoft PL-300 Certification
timelineData.description:
After leaving Novartis I worked as a freelance BI developer, delivering Power BI projects for clients — from the data model to the reports. In parallel I prepared for certification and in July 2025 earned Microsoft Certified: Data Analyst Associate (PL-300), validating my skills in preparing, modeling, visualizing, analyzing and securing data in Power BI.

See certificate
timelineData.label: Freelance · PL-300

timelineData.title: Data Analyst — Novartis Global Artwork
timelineData.description: I was a core data analyst of the international operations team. I designed and maintained reporting dashboards, developed analytical tools, and established KPIs to monitor performance. I led process-optimization projects, supported SAP workflow integrations, and delivered actionable insights that influenced strategic decisions.
timelineData.label: Novartis — Data Analyst

timelineData.title: Engineer's Degree — Wrocław University of Science and Technology
timelineData.description: I completed an Engineer's degree in Management Engineering with a specialization in IT Applications in Business. For my final thesis I developed an interactive R Shiny application to monitor the product-labeling process at a pharmaceutical company, which improved transparency and decision-making efficiency.
timelineData.label: Wrocław University of Science and Technology

timelineData.title: Intern — Novartis Global Artwork
timelineData.description: I supported the international operations team by assisting supervisors with daily tasks, preparing and automating recurring reports, and contributing to internal initiatives. I developed practical skills in data handling, process documentation, and cross-department communication.
timelineData.label: Novartis — Intern

timelineData.title: DataCamp Courses
timelineData.description: I completed a series of DataCamp courses covering R programming, data manipulation, data visualization, dashboard development, and introductory machine learning. I applied the acquired skills in practical analytical projects.
timelineData.label: DataCamp

timelineData.title: Warehouse Associate — Amazon Fulfillment Poland
timelineData.description: I contributed to Amazon's logistics operations in a dynamic warehouse environment. My responsibilities included stocking and consolidating inventory to maintain efficient workflows and later transitioning to order fulfillment, where I processed customer orders, sorted products, and prepared them for shipment. During this role, I gained practical experience with warehouse management systems and developed an understanding of data processes and operational metrics from the ground level.
timelineData.label: Amazon

timelineData.title: High School — Carolinum in Nysa
timelineData.description: I completed an advanced high-school curriculum focused on Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science, and English, which helped me develop strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
timelineData.label: Carolinum High School

projects.title: Projects
projects.subtitle: Selected work from Clickless — anonymized and shown on demo data — plus personal projects.

clickless-warehouse.title: Digital Warehouse — from Paper to Tablets | Power Platform
clickless-warehouse.description: Warehouse staff used to walk the floor with printed sheets, and data reached the system only after being retyped by hand. Now they work on tablets: the office posts tasks (deliveries, order picking, quality checks), and warehouse staff pick them up in the app and enter data on the spot by scanning items on the shelves. Anonymized work from Clickless, shown on demo data.
features: No more paper lists — work on tablets
Task queue from the office with priorities and due dates
Tasks picked up by warehouse staff, statuses in real time
Scanning items, locations and batches on the floor

clickless-sales.title: Sales & Financial Results Reporting | Power BI
clickless-sales.description: A multi-page report fed automatically from the ERP system. Financial results with revenue, costs and profit (including indirect and direct costs), top customers and products, inventory with a gross-profit simulation, and a regional analysis of sales and profit on a map. Anonymized work from Clickless, shown on demo data.
features: Financial results and margin by customer
Top customers and products by turnover and profit
Inventory, price history and gross-profit simulation
Regional analysis on a map with period comparison
Automatic data refresh from the ERP

esquie.title: Esquie — internal time-tracking system
esquie.description: Problem: the team serves a very diverse set of clients and has specific time-tracking needs, while off-the-shelf tools were expensive and awkward — they forced a rigid way of working that made logging hours a chore. Solution: an app built with a vibe-coding approach (AI-assisted), rolled out step by step — from a calendar for one person to the tool that became the core of how the company works. Tasks are planned in a calendar, completed ones turn into logged hours, and the hours report and workload views show time per project, person and period.
features: Weekly and monthly calendar with drag & drop and recurring tasks
Projects shared across the team with permissions
Hours report by project and day, CSV export
Burndown and workload views — actual vs planned time, per-person load
Node.js/Express backend on PostgreSQL with schema migrations
Three-layer backups and a dev environment with a production copy
Git repository, testing stage: smoke tests and output comparison with the previous version

project8.title: Poland through the Eyes of Eurostat Data — Energy Analysis
project8.description: An exploratory data analysis of Poland’s energy production, consumption, and sources between 2008–2022, based on Eurostat API data. The project positions Poland in the EU context, comparing key metrics with other member states, and visualizes trends, dependencies, and inefficiencies in the country’s energy sector.

project9.title: Poland — Facts and Curiosities from Wikipedia
project9.description: A data-driven overview of Poland, created through web scraping from Wikipedia (English and Polish versions). The report presents selected facts and curiosities about the country’s geography, population, language, history, economy, religion, major cities, and sports culture, combining statistical insights with cultural highlights. Each data point is sourced and linked to its original page.

project10.title: Solar Farm Analysis
project10.description: A data-driven evaluation of a 5.6 kWh residential solar farm, including automated data collection, cleaning, and performance analysis to assess efficiency, seasonal trends, and the impact of outages

testimonials.title: Testimonials
testimonials.subtitle: What clients I have delivered projects for, and people I have mentored, say.

quote: For over a year we have been working with the Clickless team on Power BI projects – both implementing solutions and developing our team's skills through training.

From the very beginning we have valued the professionalism, partnership approach and great flexibility of the Clickless team. It is a partner that listens carefully to our needs and is open to feedback, while actively proposing solutions and sharing knowledge and hands-on experience.

Smooth communication, commitment and the ability to translate our business needs into concrete, useful Power BI solutions deserve special mention. Thanks to this, the cooperation is not limited to delivering projects – it genuinely helps us make better use of data and build competences within the organization.
We can wholeheartedly recommend the Clickless team as a professional and committed partner – for Power BI implementations as well as training and development projects.

mentoring.quote: The scope of the material is well thought out and perfectly chosen — after the training you feel ready to handle real responsibilities at work, like optimizing code or solving problems under deadline pressure. He is a professional with huge knowledge and a great teacher at the same time — he presents every hard topic so clearly that even a beginner quickly gets it.

mentoring.quote: What I value most is the individual approach, the critical analysis of ideas and concrete support in solving problems. Michał helps you structure a topic and reach the best solution instead of handing out ready-made answers. His very up-to-date knowledge of AI is a big plus too. After the first five hours I decided to continue.
mentoring.author: Sylwia M.

mentoring.quote: Mentoring with Michał was very valuable. Thanks to the individual approach and practical examples, learning Power BI became much easier and more structured. Michał patiently explains even complex topics, answers questions and adapts the pace to the participant. I strongly recommend this mentoring to anyone who wants to learn Power BI effectively.
mentoring.author: Sylwia W.

quote: Mentoring with Michał gave me a lot in terms of hands-on work and a better understanding of the topics I was working on. A big plus for me was that we worked on practical tasks and examples.

I especially appreciate the concrete feedback on my work. It helped me notice things I had not spotted before, organize my knowledge and look at some issues from a different perspective. Along the way I also discovered many new tools and possibilities I had not used before. The sessions were relaxed, practical and really gave me a lot. I strongly recommend this mentoring to anyone who wants to broaden their knowledge and learn new things.

mentoring.quote: I just had my first interview for a data analyst role and it went brilliantly — both the technical part and the soft skills. They asked me about SQL, then dug into the details and into data modeling — they were very happy with my answers. Our sessions are already paying off.

consent.title: A quick note about cookies
consent.text: I count visits anonymously (no cookies, no personal data) to know how many people stop by. If you agree, I'll also turn on Google Analytics, which shows me which sections people find most interesting. Without consent the site works exactly the same.
